author: reek
body: A whitted-style ray tracer as a [Device] compute kernel: one GPU thread per pixel casts a primary ray into a fixed scene of three analytic spheres on a checkered floor, finds the nearest hit, and shades it with a rotating key light and a hard shadow ray. This is the reference site's "compute shader ray tracing" technique, generated entirely from Codex [Device] AST.

author: reek
body: The scene is data-driven: the sphere table is a set of if-ladder accessors (sphere index -> centre / radius / colour), so the nearest-hit search and the shadow test are tail-recursive folds over the object index -- the plug lowers them to WGSL loops. Real math (real-sqrt, real-sin, real-cos, real-min, real-max) comes from Gpu chapter DeviceMath; integer conversion uses the real-from-int / real-to-int builtins.

author: reek
body: Object ids 0, 1, 2 are spheres; id 3 is the floor plane at y = -1. The sphere table is fixed at compile time via if-ladder accessors.

author: reek
body: Fold over object index carrying the best id and its t; tail-recursive -> loop. Returns the nearest object id, or -1 on a full miss. t is recovered by re-intersecting the winner (cheap, avoids returning a pair).

author: reek
body: Any sphere between the hit point and the light puts the point in shadow. Fold over the three spheres; return 1 if occluded.

author: reek
body: Checker parity from truncated floor coordinates (offset to stay positive in view, so truncation behaves like floor).

author: reek
body: Per pixel: build the primary ray, find the nearest hit, compute the surface normal and albedo, then Lambert shade with a rotating key light and a hard shadow ray. Misses draw the sky gradient.
